newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Iberian bonds seen closing gap on Bunds.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Iberian bonds seen closing gap on Bunds.

text.p: Iberia's fixed-rate bonds should outperform the German Bunds in the coming week as calm returns to the peseta and escudo and the Italian market recovers its poise, analysts said.
The spread between Iberia's benchmark 10-year cash issues and the Bund should narrow back to around 110 basis points from the current level around 120, they said.

But the greatest interest, and therefore the greatest potential for improvement, will be in the two-year sector which suffered most from the recent bout of nerves about southern Europe's chances of qualifying for monetary union.

As a result, the yield curves in Spain and Portugal should steepen, something which would be compatible with expectations of further rate cuts by the Bank of Spain and Portugal even if they do not come immediately, the analysts said.

"The spreads between Portugal and Spain and Germany, in the long and the short end of the curve, can narrow. The 10-year could fall to around 110 basis points in the coming week," said analyst Valentin Fernandez of Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
"If things improve in Italy, it may be possible to see levels below 110 basis points," said Nuno Godinho of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Lisbon.

But a word of caution came from Serge Goncalves of Finmat in London who, despite predicting a narrowing of spreads, doubted that the peseta and the escudo would gain much on the mark in the coming week.
Analysts said the slippage of Spain and Portugal in the past week had shown good support for the longer end at 125-130 basis points above the German equivalent.

The current spread of some 119 basis points compares with a record low of between 83 and 80 basis points hit when euphoria over the two countries' chances of joining the single currency was at its height at the end of January.

The spreads widened after northern political and business leaders expressed doubts that the so-called 'Club Med' countries -- Italy, Spain and Portugal -- would or should gain entry to monetary union at the start in January 1999.

"The Club Med was heavily penalised this week. As the Iberian currencies quieten down, the Bonos and the OT (Portuguese bonds) could take aboard some of the gains made by the Italian BTP on Thursday," said one London trader.
Italy's futures have jumped 140 basis points since their Wednesday close. After gaining limited ground on Thursday, both Spain and Portugal were easier on Friday.
Fernandez said however that the biggest advance should be in the shorter end of the curve.
"It is the moment to look at the fundamentals...they are good in Iberia, and think in new rate cuts by the central banks, but without the euphoria of the beginning of the year," he said.
The Spanish and Portuguese two-year bonds are presently trading at a premium of 209 and 218 basis points above their German equivalents.
The spread between the Spanish and Portuguese markets at the short end was natural given the fact that Bank of Portugal rates were higher than those in Spain.
"The two-year spread between Spain and the Bund could go to around 200 basis points, which would be coherent with some renewed expectations of a cut in Spanish rates," said Fernandez.
"I expect to see the spread between 195 and 200 basis points in the coming week," said the London trader.
After the good inflation news in January, the Bank of Spain could opt to cut its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75 percent as soon as the peseta recovered some strength, Fernandez said.
But Godinho saw no cut by the Bank of Spain, even with the peseta calm again, before March, with the Bank of Portugal moving later.
--Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
